stage1.impression: A warm late-afternoon living room with convincing raking sun on the plaster, sensible restraint and clear space for type on the wall. The pair itself reads as CG, though: the cabinets are acid, almost fluorescent green with the interior reading as solid lime plastic blocks, the woofer discs are dead-flat matte circles, and a near-white popcorn-textured rug is the brightest thing in the frame, pulling the eye to the bottom edge. The credenza's veneer is streaky and stretched.

blocking_9: Cabinets read as tinted glass/acrylic, not fluorescent plastic: lit cabinet regions within dE2000 18 of #B2C9A2 with a blue channel above ~60, not near 0
Woofer cover shows light modelling (a gradient across the disc), not a flat fill
The rug (or whatever is in the foreground) is darker than the sunlit wall and has a believable, non-noisy pile
Credenza veneer shows real walnut figure with no stretched or streaked texture
The cabinets' green transmitted light lands visibly on the floor or wall beside each speaker, so they plainly sit in the sun
The exterior through the glazing reads as a sharp real view, not a soft low-res plate

defects.what: Left cabinet acid green, b_median 6-40; interior batts read as solid lime plastic blocks, not lit voile/polyester
Right cabinet: same oversaturated acid green
Woofer cover disc is uniformly flat (lum_range 3.0), reads as a CG circle
Rug is the brightest object (lum_median 221 vs sun-lit wall 215) and its texture reads as a noisy popcorn pattern
Credenza walnut veneer reads as horizontally stretched streaks, not wood figure
Exterior forest view soft and low on detail; reads as a blurred backplate
No green transmitted light reaches the floor beside the speakers (114,94,65 is plain warm floor)
Window frame base corner crushed (crush 1.9%), slightly murky
The upper-right wall is busy with a large shadow trapezoid, a bright patch and a horn shadow cut by the edge, competing with the right speaker

changes.problem: The cabinets render as fluorescent lime with almost no blue, so they read as plastic rather than as a $20k tinted acrylic and miss their reference colour.

change.to: sun #FFEAD4, white_balance_k 5000 (keep exposure -0.9); if still acid, add a -10% saturation on greens in the grade only

changes.expected: Cabinet lit areas move toward pale sage with blue around 70-90, and the wall keeps a warm but less orange cast.

changes.problem: The rug is the brightest and noisiest surface in the frame and pulls the eye away from the pair to the bottom edge.

evidence.measured: lum_median 220.7 (sunlit wall 215.1), RGB 234,220,191; popcorn pile texture visible at 1x

change.to: a low-pile flatweave wool texture, value 0.3, tint #7A6E60, size [2.2, 1.6], position [0.0, -1.5]

changes.expected: The rug drops to a mid-tone strip below the speakers and stops competing; the pair and wall become the brightest areas.

changes.problem: The woofer covers are lit flat from the front, so they read as painted CG circles with no form.

evidence.measured: lum_range 3.0, lum_p5 81.4 / p95 84.4; RGB 64,93,45, dE 7.8 vs #2E4A2C (too light)

change.to: irradiance 0.06, position [-2.0, -3.8, 1.8] (move the fill to the window side so it models from the left)

changes.expected: The disc darkens toward its reference and shows a gentle left-to-right gradient.

changes.problem: The credenza's walnut veneer reads as horizontally stretched streaks, which says 'render' in the middle of the frame.

evidence.measured: 2x crop shows long uniform horizontal streaks with no cathedral or straight-grain figure

change.to: grain_rot 0.0 (grain running horizontally at true scale, not stretched), or a different walnut veneer scan at 4k with UVs scaled per door

changes.expected: The doors show readable walnut grain with figure, no streaking.

changes.problem: The sun passes through the cabinets, but their green light barely shows on the floor, so the pair doesn't visibly sit in the light.

evidence.measured: floor RGB 114,94,65, no green; the green patch shows only faintly on the wall by the vase [915,430,950,480]

change.to: azimuth -72, elevation 20 (lands the transmitted pool on the floor just right of each cabinet, inside the frame)

changes.expected: A soft green-tinted pool on the floorboards right of each speaker, g_median above r_median there.

changes.problem: The view through the glazing is soft and low on detail and reads as a backplate.

evidence.measured: 2x crop: branches smeared, no fine twig detail

change.to: blur 0.0, strength 2.6 (a touch less bright so the curtain edge holds)

changes.expected: Sharper tree detail outside without blowing the window.

changes.problem: The upper-right wall has a busy shadow trapezoid and a cut-off horn shadow, which pulls attention from the right speaker and unbalances the space for type.

evidence.measured: shadow lum 105.6 against a sun patch of 192 at the right edge [1270,455,1440,480]; a partial horn silhouette at the edge

change.from: window 2 along -0.45 m (its frame throws the trapezoid)
change.to: window 2 along -0.9 m, or close that bay with the drape, so the right-hand wall falls into one even shadow

changes.expected: One calm shadow area on the right wall behind the right speaker, with the left-to-centre sun patch left as the heading's field.

changes.problem: The base of the window frame in the bottom-left corner is crushed and murky.

change.to: lift blacks so the floor shadow holds detail (toe +0.02)

changes.expected: The corner keeps some floorboard detail.

out_of_scope.request: Give the woofer cover a visible cloth weave or texture instead of a flat solid disc
out_of_scope.why: It is the speaker's material (cover cloth); fixed per the card.

out_of_scope.request: Make the interior batts read as soft polyester in voile sleeves rather than solid lime blocks
out_of_scope.why: It is the speaker's internal material and shading; fixed. Only the light and grade (c1) may help.

out_of_scope.request: Lower the acrylic's saturation at the material level if the grade cannot reach #B2C9A2
out_of_scope.why: It is the speaker's colour; fixed.
